title: Done Means: make completion checkable
subtitle: An evidence-backed finish line for projects that need to ship

intro.label: OPERATING GUIDE
intro.title: A project is finished when an observer can prove it
intro.subtitle: Define the finish line, trace every task to it, and verify the result
intro.summary: Done Means is a disciplined audit and execution method for replacing vague status with independently checkable conditions. It keeps evidence, judgment, and action separate.

methodology.label: METHOD
methodology.title: Completion is a proof problem
body: Read the live project before forming an opinion. Turn the finish line into conditions an independent observer can check.
Only observed failures, explicit absences, and required finish-line work become tasks. Every task carries evidence, a dependency, and a testable acceptance statement.

items.title: Define DONE MEANS
items.headline: Replace vague completion language with conditions an observer can check
items.thesis: A finish line names the command, URL, route, file, behavior, or recorded result that must be true.
items.whyBody: Terms such as polished or production ready hide disagreement. A checkable condition exposes the actual gap and gives the next task a precise target.
items.takeaway: Write three to six conditions before writing a backlog.

verdict.fit: Projects with ambiguous status or competing definitions of done
verdict.whyNow: A precise finish line prevents activity from being mistaken for progress.
verdict.nextStep: Write the conditions in the project's own language.

highlights.title: Name the proof
highlights.body: Use a command, route, URL, file, behavior, or recorded result.

highlights.title: Drop the fog
highlights.body: If an independent observer cannot check it, rewrite it.

tabs.label: MECHANICS
tabs.title: A good condition is observable
tabs.body: Use a statement such as `npm run build exits 0`, `GET /health returns 200`, or `a logged-out user reaches the dashboard`. Avoid `works correctly`.

highlights.title: Acceptance
highlights.body: The condition says what someone can inspect.

items.title: Read the project
items.headline: Prior reports are claims until the live project confirms them
items.thesis: Read instructions, manifests, configuration, source entry points, tests, and Git state before deciding what remains.
items.whyBody: A roadmap built from stale notes can send work in the wrong direction. The live tree is the source for current evidence, dependencies, and failures.
items.takeaway: Declare what you read, sampled, and skipped.

verdict.fit: Any project with handoffs, parallel agents, or stale status notes
verdict.whyNow: The cheapest way to avoid a false backlog is to inspect first.
risks: Skipping source and tests creates stale tasks.
verdict.nextStep: Run the project's own verification commands.

highlights.title: Read in order
highlights.body: Docs, instructions, manifests, config, source, tests, Git.

highlights.title: Record coverage
highlights.body: State which directories were read, sampled, or skipped.

tabs.label: PROOF
tabs.title: Run the commands that prove it
tabs.body: Use the project's documented build, typecheck, lint, test, or smoke-test commands. Capture actual output and errors instead of paraphrasing them.

highlights.title: No guessing
highlights.body: A passing document is not a passing system.

tabs.label: DECISION
tabs.title: Trust current evidence over old status

items.title: Classify the gap
items.headline: Every task must be BROKEN, MISSING, or REQUIRED
items.thesis: The three finding types prevent generic cleanup from entering a finish-line roadmap.
items.whyBody: A broken feature needs a failure citation. A missing surface needs a reference and absence. Required work needs a finish-line condition. The classification forces the evidence to stay specific.
items.takeaway: If the evidence does not fit one source, do not add the task.

verdict.fit: Audits where backlog padding is a recurring failure
verdict.whyNow: A narrow finding taxonomy keeps the roadmap short and defensible.
risks: Generic best practice becomes unbounded scope.
verdict.nextStep: Attach one evidence citation to each finding.

highlights.title: BROKEN
highlights.body: Something exists and you observed it fail.

highlights.title: REQUIRED
highlights.body: The finish line needs work with no implementation reference.

tabs.label: MECHANICS
tabs.title: Evidence is a locator
tabs.body: Cite a path and line, a command and error, or an explicit absence. A sentence that merely repeats the finding is not evidence.

highlights.title: Specificity
highlights.body: The citation should let another person recheck the claim.

items.title: Sequence the work
items.headline: Order tasks by what unlocks the next proof
items.thesis: A dependency-ordered roadmap shows the critical path and names one first task instead of presenting a flat backlog.
items.whyBody: A task can be real and still be the wrong next action. Dependencies expose blockers, parallel work, and the first safe move.
items.takeaway: Name phases for outcomes, not categories.

verdict.fit: Multi-phase builds with blocked or parallel work
verdict.whyNow: Sequence is where an audit becomes an operating plan.
risks: Flat lists hide the critical path.
verdict.nextStep: Assign each task a phase and dependency set.

highlights.title: Outcome names
highlights.body: Use names such as Local build runs green.

highlights.title: Independent proof
highlights.body: Split work until each task has a clear acceptance test.

tabs.label: MECHANICS
tabs.title: Make progress visible
tabs.body: Each task carries a done-when statement, dependency list, effort, risk, and confidence. That makes handoff and review possible without guesswork.

items.title: Execute against proof
items.headline: A written task is not complete until its acceptance condition passes
items.thesis: Execute the smallest safe change, rerun the relevant check, and update the existing record with current evidence.
items.whyBody: Files can be written while the real route, build, deployment, or user behavior remains broken. Completion is an independent recheck of each condition.
items.takeaway: Verify the outcome, not the activity.

verdict.fit: Projects where status often means attempted rather than proven
verdict.whyNow: The verification gate is what separates a roadmap from decoration.
risks: Command success can mask a failed user outcome.

highlights.title: Smallest change
highlights.body: Avoid unrelated cleanup and scope expansion.

highlights.title: Fresh evidence
highlights.body: Update the task record with the current proof.

tabs.label: PROOF
tabs.title: Recheck the finish line
tabs.body: Do not inherit completion from a task status. Re-run the check that the condition names, then record what passed and what remains.

highlights.title: Outcome first
highlights.body: The user-visible result is the load-bearing proof.

items.title: Stop honestly
items.headline: A real blocker is a valid result when the evidence is clear
items.thesis: Stop at missing access, approval, credentials, safety boundaries, or external systems instead of manufacturing certainty.
items.whyBody: A clean unresolved report protects the next operator. It names the blocker, owner, clearing action, and cheapest unblocker without pretending the project is complete.
items.takeaway: Unresolved with proof is better than complete without it.

verdict.fit: Any workflow with external approvals or production boundaries
verdict.whyNow: Honest stopping keeps the finish line trustworthy.
risks: False completion pushes hidden work downstream.
verdict.nextStep: Record the blocker and its clearing action.

highlights.title: Name the owner
highlights.body: Say who must clear the decision or access gap.

highlights.title: Preserve trust
highlights.body: Do not call an attempted action a verified outcome.

tabs.label: DECISION
tabs.title: Stop at the boundary
tabs.body: When the next action needs approval, credentials, external access, or a production change, record the boundary and hand off the clearing action.

tabs.label: SOURCE
tabs.title: Inspect the public package
tabs.body: The public package contains the portable workflow, references, launch prompts, and an uploadable ZIP.

closing.label: NEXT
closing.title: Run one audit on a live project
body: Name the project, finish-line source, and roadmap backend. Then let the evidence decide what remains.
The method is portable because it does not assume a private tracker, filesystem, account, or deployment target.

seo.title: Done Means: make completion checkable
seo.description: An evidence-backed guide to defining, sequencing, executing, and verifying project completion.
